text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- American support to Bosnia is conditional upon opening towns to all people, regardless of their religion or nationality, former U.S. senator Bob Dole said during visit to Sarajevo.

- NATO General Secretary Javier Solana, during a visit to Bosnia, called for promoting confidence between armies in both entities and urged the formation of a joint military committee which has yet to be established.

- A group of five Moslem families moved back to the Croat-controlled town of Stolac, the first such return since the war ended, says Moslem-Croat federation ministry for refugees and displaced persons.

- The OSCE mission says it closed a voter registration centre in Zepce because of suspected irregularities after supervisors found an unusually high number displaced persons' applications in the period between June 7-12.
- If the Moslem-Croat federation fails to agree new municipalities, the country may face fresh divisions, federation minister of justice, Mato Tadic, says.

- The Moslem-Croat federation army will number 45,000 soldiers in peacetime with the national ratio between Moslems and Croats at 2.5 to 1, Sakib Mahmuljin, deputy to federation defence minister, says. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387 71 663 864
